Josephine Wright

Instructions

Answer the following questions and/or complete the exercises in RMarkdown. Please embed all of your code and push the final work to your repository. Your report should be organized, clean, and run free from errors. Remember, you must remove the # for any included code chunks to run.

Load the tidyverse

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Data

For this assignment, we will use data from a study on elephants and the effects of poaching on tusk size.

Reference: Chiyo, Patrick I., Vincent Obanda, and David K. Korir. “Illegal tusk harvest and the decline of tusk size in the African elephant.” Ecology and Evolution 5, 22: 5216–5229 (2015). Data deposited at Dryad Digital Repository.

1. Before starting data analysis, read the abstract of the paper to get an idea of the questions being asked. In 2-3 sentences, describe what the study is testing and the variables involved.

The study is testing whether or not tusk size is heritable. During the recovery of elephant populations, both the length and circumference of male and female elephants were measured and found to have decreased by significant percentages.

2. Load elephants.csv and store it as a new object called elephants.

elephants <- read_csv("data/elephants.csv")
## Rows: 777 Columns: 7
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (3): Years of sample collection, Elephant ID, Sex
## dbl (4): Estimated Age (years), shoulder Height in  cm, Tusk Length in cm, T...
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.

3. Clean the data by converting variable names to lowercase with no spaces or special characters.

elephants <- elephants %>% 
  clean_names()

7. How many males and females were sampled in this study?

elephants %>% 
  count(sex, sort=T)

##   sex       n
##   <fct> <int>

8. What is the mean, median, and standard deviation for age of males and females included in the study? Separate the results by year of sample collection. Does the sampling look even between years and sexes?

 elephants %>% 
  filter(years_of_sample_collection=="1966-68", sex=="f") %>% 
  summarize(mean_age_f_old=mean(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T),
            median_age_f_old=median(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T),
            sd_age_f_old=sd(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   mean_age_f_old median_age_f_old sd_age_f_old
##            <dbl>            <dbl>        <dbl>
## 1           17.6               15         13.6
elephants %>% 
  filter(sex=="f", years_of_sample_collection=="2005-13") %>% 
  summarize(mean_age_f_new=mean(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T),
            median_age_f_new=median(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T),
            sd_age_f_new=sd(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   mean_age_f_new median_age_f_new sd_age_f_new
##            <dbl>            <dbl>        <dbl>
## 1           17.9             17.5         11.0
elephants %>% 
  filter(sex=="m" | years_of_sample_collection=="1966-68") %>% 
  summarize(mean_age_m_old=mean(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T),
            median_age_m_old=median(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T),
            sd_age_m_old=sd(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   mean_age_m_old median_age_m_old sd_age_m_old
##            <dbl>            <dbl>        <dbl>
## 1           14.7               11         12.4
elephants %>% 
  filter(sex=="m" | years_of_sample_collection=="2005-13") %>% 
  summarize(mean_age_m_new=mean(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T),
            median_age_m_new=median(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T),
            sd_age_m_new=sd(estimated_age_years, na.rm=T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   mean_age_m_new median_age_m_new sd_age_m_new
##            <dbl>            <dbl>        <dbl>
## 1           13.3               10         10.9

The sampling appears to be even across within the sexes but not so much across years.

9. Is age (independent variable) a positive predictor of tusk length (dependent variable)? Create a plot that shows the relationship between these variables and add a linear model fit line.

elephants %>% 
  select(estimated_age_years, tusk_length_in_cm) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=estimated_age_years, y=tusk_length_in_cm))+
  geom_point(mapping=aes(color=tusk_length_in_cm))+
  geom_smooth(method=lm, se=T)+
  labs(title="tusk length (cm) vs. age (yrs)")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 182 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 182 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

Age does appear to be a positive indicator of tusk length.

10. Is shoulder height (independent variable) a positive predictor of tusk length (dependent variable)? Create a plot that shows the relationship between these variables and add a linear model fit line.

elephants %>% 
  select(shoulder_height_in_cm, tusk_length_in_cm) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=shoulder_height_in_cm, y=tusk_length_in_cm))+
  geom_point(mapping=aes(color=tusk_length_in_cm))+
  geom_smooth(method=lm, se=T)+
  labs(titles="tusk length (cm) vs. shoulder height (cm)")
## Ignoring unknown labels:
## • titles : "tusk length (cm) vs. shoulder height (cm)"
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 181 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 181 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

Yes shoulder height appears to be a positive indicator of tusk length.

11. The authors argue that because poachers preferentially target elephants with large tusks, this has resulted in a decrease in average tusk length. Is this supported by the data? Show your code and calculations below.

elephants %>% 
  filter(years_of_sample_collection=="1966-68") %>% 
  summarize(mean_tusk_length_in_cm_old=mean(tusk_length_in_cm, na.rm=T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 1
##   mean_tusk_length_in_cm_old
##                        <dbl>
## 1                       96.9
elephants %>% 
  filter(years_of_sample_collection=="2005-13") %>% 
  summarize(mean_tusk_length_in_cm_old=mean(tusk_length_in_cm, na.rm=T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 1
##   mean_tusk_length_in_cm_old
##                        <dbl>
## 1                       77.2
elephants %>% 
  select(years_of_sample_collection, tusk_length_in_cm) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=years_of_sample_collection, y=tusk_length_in_cm))+
  geom_boxplot(mapping=aes(fill=years_of_sample_collection))+
  labs(title="tusk length (cm) vs. years of sample collection")
## Warning: Removed 180 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

Yes, this is supported by the data. It can be seen in the boxplots that the median tusk length has dipped significantly.

12. Male elephants reach effective sexual maturity at 25 years while females are sexually mature at 12 years. Make a new dataframe that extracts only the males and females at sexual maturity. Then, make a plot that shows the range of tusk length between the two sample periods for these mature elephants.

elephants_mature <- elephants %>% 
  filter(sex=="f" & estimated_age_years>=12 | sex=="m" & estimated_age_years>=25)

elephants_mature
## # A tibble: 289 × 7
##    years_of_sample_collection elephant_id sex   estimated_age_years
##    <fct>                      <fct>       <fct>               <dbl>
##  1 1966-68                    67          f                    12  
##  2 1966-68                    7           f                    13  
##  3 1966-68                    15          f                    13  
##  4 1966-68                    164         f                    13  
##  5 1966-68                    237         f                    13  
##  6 1966-68                    194         f                    13.5
##  7 1966-68                    23          f                    14  
##  8 1966-68                    148         f                    14  
##  9 1966-68                    204         f                    14  
## 10 1966-68                    219         f                    14  
## # ℹ 279 more rows
## # ℹ 3 more variables: shoulder_height_in_cm <dbl>, tusk_length_in_cm <dbl>,
## #   tusk_circumference_in_cm <dbl>
elephants_mature %>% 
  select(tusk_length_in_cm, years_of_sample_collection) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=years_of_sample_collection, y=tusk_length_in_cm))+
  geom_boxplot(mapping=aes(fill=years_of_sample_collection))+
  labs(title="tusk length (cm) vs years of sample collection in mature elephants")
